title: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 13 2024
description: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 13 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: I really enjoy ___ difficult grammar problems.
questions.explanation: Enjoy is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: She decided ___ abroad after graduation.
questions.explanation: Decide is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: They are interested in ___ a new language.
questions.explanation: A verb after a preposition takes the gerund form.

questions.questionText: He ___ driving at night whenever possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: ___ regularly requires considerable discipline.
questions.explanation: The gerund exercising functions as the subject.

questions.questionText: Swimming ___ excellent physical exercise.
questions.explanation: A gerund phrase functioning as the subject normally takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: She is exceptionally good at ___ complicated problems.
questions.explanation: At is a preposition and is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: He left without ___ goodbye to anyone.
questions.explanation: Without is a preposition and is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Before ___ the laboratory, make sure all the equipment is switched off.
questions.explanation: Before is followed by a gerund when used as a preposition.

questions.questionText: Thank you for ___ me with the assignment.
questions.explanation: For is a preposition, so helping is required.

questions.questionText: The committee suggested ___ the examination until next week.
questions.explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: The company is considering ___ its headquarters to another city.
questions.explanation: Consider is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: He finally finished ___ the research report.
questions.explanation: Finish is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Do you mind ___ the door while I am working?
questions.explanation: Mind is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: She spends several hours ___ English every evening.
questions.explanation: Spend time is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: He admitted ___ the confidential information.
questions.explanation: Admit is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: She denied ___ the money from the office.
questions.explanation: Deny is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Don't risk ___ your entire investment.
questions.explanation: Risk is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: I can't stand ___ in crowded places for hours.
questions.explanation: Can't stand is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: She couldn't help ___ when she heard the story.
questions.explanation: Can't help is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: I don't feel like ___ out tonight.
questions.explanation: Feel like is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: After years of trying, he finally gave up ___.
questions.explanation: Give up is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: I look forward to ___ from you soon.
questions.explanation: In look forward to, to is a preposition and therefore takes a gerund.

questions.questionText: The documentary is well worth ___.
questions.explanation: Be worth is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: She has considerable difficulty ___ technical instructions.
questions.explanation: Have difficulty is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: He wants ___ medicine at university.
questions.explanation: Want is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: You need ___ more carefully before making a decision.
questions.explanation: Need is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: They hope ___ the competition next year.
questions.explanation: Hope is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She promised ___ the documents before Friday.
questions.explanation: Promise is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The suspect refused ___ any questions.
questions.explanation: Refuse is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The researchers expect ___ the results by Friday.
questions.explanation: Expect is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She offered ___ us with the difficult task.
questions.explanation: Offer is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: He managed ___ the problem without assistance.
questions.explanation: Manage is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She could not afford ___ a new laptop.
questions.explanation: Afford is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: He learned ___ a car when he was eighteen.
questions.explanation: Learn is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She plans ___ her studies next year.
questions.explanation: Plan is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: I went to the library ___ for the entrance examination.
questions.explanation: The to-infinitive expresses the purpose of the action.

questions.questionText: She saved money ___ a new computer.
questions.explanation: To buy expresses purpose and means 'in order to buy'.

questions.questionText: He called the manager ___ about the delayed payment.
questions.explanation: The infinitive expresses the purpose of calling.

questions.questionText: I want you ___ the instructions carefully.
questions.explanation: Want can be followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The teacher asked the students ___ quietly.
questions.explanation: Ask is followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The doctor advised him ___ more water.
questions.explanation: Advise is followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The coach encouraged the players ___ harder.
questions.explanation: Encourage is followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She reminded me ___ the application before midnight.
questions.explanation: Remind is followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: They invited us ___ the ceremony.
questions.explanation: Invite is followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The teacher allowed the students ___ early.
questions.explanation: Allow is followed by object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She can ___ three languages fluently.
questions.explanation: A modal verb is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: You must ___ your identification card at the entrance.
questions.explanation: Must is a modal verb and takes the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: Students should ___ the instructions before answering.
questions.explanation: Should is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: They will ___ the results tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Will is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: The teacher made the student ___ the answer again.
questions.explanation: Make is followed by object + bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: His parents let him ___ abroad alone.
questions.explanation: Let is followed by object + bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: She likes ___ historical novels in her free time.
questions.explanation: Like can be followed by either a gerund or a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She likes ___ historical novels in her free time.
questions.explanation: Like can be followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: He loves ___ early in the morning.
questions.explanation: Love can be followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: He hates ___ for unreliable transportation.
questions.explanation: Hate can be followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: I prefer ___ rather than driving through heavy traffic.
questions.explanation: Prefer can be followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: I prefer ___ rather than drive through heavy traffic.
questions.explanation: Prefer can also be followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: When the doctor arrived, the patient stopped ___.
questions.explanation: Stop + gerund means to end or quit the activity.

questions.questionText: He stopped ___ because he needed to make an urgent phone call.
questions.explanation: Stop + gerund means cease the activity.

questions.questionText: He stopped ___ a phone call on his way home.
questions.explanation: Stop + infinitive means stop one activity in order to do another.

questions.questionText: I remember ___ him at the conference several years ago.
questions.explanation: Remember + gerund refers to remembering a past action.

questions.questionText: Remember ___ the laboratory door before you leave.
questions.explanation: Remember + infinitive refers to remembering a duty that must be done.

questions.questionText: I will never forget ___ the ocean for the first time.
questions.explanation: Forget + gerund refers to a past experience.

questions.questionText: She forgot ___ the electricity bill before leaving.
questions.explanation: Forget + infinitive means fail to remember an action that should be done.

questions.questionText: Try ___ the application again if the first attempt fails.
questions.explanation: Try + gerund means experiment with a method.

questions.questionText: He tried ___ the heavy box, but it was too difficult.
questions.explanation: Try + infinitive means make an effort to do something.

questions.questionText: I regret ___ such harsh words during the argument.
questions.explanation: Regret + gerund expresses sorrow about a past action.

questions.questionText: We regret ___ you that the position has already been filled.
questions.explanation: Regret + infinitive is used formally to announce bad news.

questions.questionText: This position means ___ late several times a week.
questions.explanation: Mean + gerund means involve or result in.

questions.questionText: I meant ___ you yesterday, but I became extremely busy.
questions.explanation: Mean + infinitive means intend to do something.

questions.questionText: She went on ___ about the same problem for another hour.
questions.explanation: Go on + gerund means continue the same activity.

questions.questionText: After discussing the first theory, the professor went on ___ the second.
questions.explanation: Go on + infinitive means begin a different or subsequent action.

questions.questionText: I am happy ___ you with the application.
questions.explanation: Adjectives describing feelings or reactions commonly take a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The instructions were difficult ___ without additional explanation.
questions.explanation: Difficult is commonly followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She is afraid of ___ the wrong decision.
questions.explanation: Of is a preposition, so the following verb takes the gerund.

questions.questionText: He is ready ___ the examination.
questions.explanation: Ready is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: She is interested in ___ computer programming.
questions.explanation: In is a preposition, so learning is required.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Enjoy is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Want is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: He is good at to play football.
He is good at playing football.
He is good at play football.
He is good to playing football.
questions.explanation: At is a preposition and must be followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: I look forward to meet you.
I look forward to meeting you.
I look forward to met you.
questions.explanation: The to in look forward to is a preposition and takes a gerund.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Make is followed by object + bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: She can to swim very well.
questions.explanation: Can is a modal verb and is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: Reading and ___ are essential skills for academic success.
questions.explanation: Parallel structures require the same grammatical form: reading and writing.

questions.questionText: The student hopes to pass the exam and ___ a scholarship.
questions.explanation: The coordinated verbs are both expressed with to-infinitives.

questions.questionText: She enjoys reading novels and ___ academic articles.
questions.explanation: The parallel structure requires two gerunds.

questions.questionText: He decided to study harder and ___ less time on social media.
questions.explanation: After decided to study, the coordinated verb can share the infinitive marker: to study and spend.

questions.questionText: ___ in the morning and ___ regularly can improve concentration.
questions.explanation: Both activities function as subjects and require parallel gerunds.

questions.questionText: The manager asked the assistant ___ the files and ___ the report.
questions.explanation: Ask takes object + to-infinitive, and the two actions are parallel.

questions.questionText: She spent the afternoon ___ for the exam instead of ___ television.
questions.explanation: Spend time and instead of both require gerund forms in this structure.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an infinitive to express purpose?
options: He went to the library studying.
He went to the library to study.
He went to the library study.
He went to the library studied.
questions.explanation: To study expresses the purpose of going to the library.

questions.questionText: She opened the window ___ some fresh air into the room.
questions.explanation: The infinitive expresses the purpose of opening the window.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a verb followed by a gerund?
questions.explanation: Consider is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a verb followed by an infinitive?
questions.explanation: Decide is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The professor encouraged the students ___ more critically.
questions.explanation: Encourage takes object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The security officer told everyone ___ the building immediately.
questions.explanation: Tell takes object + to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The new regulations require employees ___ protective equipment.
questions.explanation: In this structure, employees are followed by the to-infinitive.

questions.questionText: The teacher did not allow the students ___ their phones during the test.
questions.explanation: Allow takes object + to-infinitive.
